name: CapCut Color-Change Highlight Wipe
use_when: A short title, quote, claim, or documentary-style statement needs a premium highlight pass.
The editor wants the highlighted area to invert or change the text color as it travels across the words.
The text can sit on a controlled background or card where a rectangular highlight feels intentional.
avoid_when: The phrase is long or dense enough that the wipe delays comprehension.
The highlight bar covers faces, proof, UI, or product details.
The color change lowers contrast in either the highlighted or non-highlighted state.
The line needs plain captions rather than designed emphasis text.

timeline_pattern.pattern: base_background -> base_text -> duplicate_text_above_highlight_bar -> inverted_text_color -> compound_top_text_and_bar -> Split_mask_90deg -> start_keyframe_off_left -> end_keyframe_off_right -> ease_keyframes -> qc
timeline_pattern.layer_rule: The base and inverted text layers must match position, font, size, tracking, and line breaks so the color change feels like one text object.
timeline_pattern.highlight_rule: Resize the highlight background to the phrase instead of using a full-screen block.
timeline_pattern.hold_rule: Let the phrase establish before the wipe starts when the highlight is a reveal rather than an instant emphasis.

motion.rule: The split mask should travel smoothly across the highlight bar and clear before the next reading task begins.

keyframe_values.mask_rotation: Set the Split mask around 90 degrees for a horizontal left-to-right highlight wipe.
keyframe_values.start_position: Start the split mask fully off the left side of the highlight area.
keyframe_values.end_position: End the split mask fully off the right side of the highlight area.
keyframe_values.easing: Apply easing to both mask keyframes so the highlight feels deliberate rather than mechanical.
keyframe_values.delay: A short pre-wipe hold, such as about 1 second in a calm title, can let the statement register before the highlight moves.

sound.rule: Use no sound or one soft tick/brush cue on the highlight start only if it does not compete with speech.

captions.rule: Suppress ordinary captions in the same region if the highlight text already carries the spoken words.

color.rule: The base and highlighted states both need strong contrast; black/white inversion works only when it matches the design tone.

implementation.ffmpeg: Create base text with drawtext or a pre-rendered layer, composite a duplicate inverted/highlighted text group through an animated grayscale alpha mask using alphamerge, then inspect start/mid/hold/clear frames for alignment drift and alpha leakage.
implementation.remotion: Build a HighlightWipeText component with absolute base/styled text layers, CSS mask-image or clip-path progress from off-left to off-right, highlightRect, easing, captionSuppression metadata, and optional transparent ProRes export.
implementation.blender: Use duplicate text objects and an animated rectangular mask or wipe plane to reveal the inverted/highlighted text layer.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Place base text, duplicate the text above a custom-sized highlight background, invert the top text color, compound the top text plus highlight, add Video > Mask > Split, rotate to 90 degrees, keyframe the mask from left to right, and ease both keyframes.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Graphics duplicate text over a shape layer, nest the highlighted version, animate a linear wipe or mask, and verify text layer alignment.

common_mistakes: Misaligning the base and highlighted text layers so the letters jump during the wipe.
Using a highlight bar that is too large and covers unrelated visual information.
Choosing highlight colors that look premium but reduce edge contrast.
Letting the wipe start before the viewer can read the phrase.
Leaving duplicate captions underneath the highlighted text.
qc: Do the base and highlighted text layers align perfectly?
Does the highlight preserve readable contrast during the entire wipe?
Does the mask start and end outside the highlighted phrase?
Is the phrase readable before and after the wipe?
Do captions, faces, proof, UI, products, and action remain safe?
If exported as an overlay, does the file preserve alpha instead of rendering a black box?
